title: Prism Axis
description: Axis configuration for a position channel.

axis.description: Axis options including title, ticks, grid, and label placement. Null suppresses the axis entirely (no domain line, ticks, labels, title or grid) and releases the padding its side reserved — omitting the `axis` key instead keeps the default axis.

orient.description: Side of the chart on which the axis appears.

tick_count.description: How many major ticks to aim for on a continuous axis (linear, log, pow, sqrt, time). A hint, not a guarantee: the generator rounds to a readable step and may land either side of the request. Omit for the default of 5; 0 removes every tick. Grid lines sit at the major tick positions, so this also controls how many grid lines appear. Ignored on discrete (band / point / ordinal) axes, which tick once per category.

tick_min_step.description: Smallest gap, in domain units, allowed between adjacent generated ticks. Enforced by asking the generator for fewer ticks so the survivors stay round. Shapes generated ticks only - `values` pins exactly what it names.

values.description: Explicit tick set, replacing the generated one and overriding `tick_count` and `tick_min_step`. Numbers on a quantitative axis, ISO-8601 date strings (or epoch milliseconds) on a temporal axis, exact category names on a discrete one. Entries outside the resolved scale domain are dropped with PRISM_WARN_AXIS_VALUES_DROPPED rather than drawn off-plot. Grid lines follow the pinned set; minor ticks are suppressed.

grid.description: Whether to draw grid lines. Grid lines sit at the major tick positions, so `tick_count`, `values` and `tick_min_step` choose *which* ones appear; this key only turns the whole set on or off.

label_angle.description: Rotation angle in degrees for tick labels.

label_padding.description: Padding between axis and labels in pixels.

label_limit.description: Maximum allowed label pixel width before truncation.

domain.description: Whether to draw the axis domain line.

zindex.description: Stacking order relative to other chart elements.
